questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Compare House and Senate term lengths
questions.stem: A beekeeper logs colony inspections; House members serve how many years?
questions.explanation: House members serve two-year terms. Senate members serve six-year terms. The difference shapes electoral responsiveness.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper tracks honey sold across state lines; why can Congress regulate it?

answer.exemplar: The Commerce Clause grants Congress power to regulate interstate trade, so goods crossing state lines fall under federal authority.

questions.explanation: Commerce power covers trade among states. It prevents conflicting state trade barriers.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT

stimulus.body: Congress has enumerated powers plus authority to make laws necessary and proper to execute them. This clause supports institutions like a national bank.

questions.stem: A beekeeper's cooperative creates a shared storage facility not explicitly listed; which clause supports it?

options.text: The Supremacy Clause creates new powers
The Necessary and Proper Clause supports executing enumerated powers
The Tenth Amendment reserves all new powers
The Commerce Clause only regulates foreign trade

questions.explanation: Implied powers flow from the Necessary and Proper Clause, letting Congress execute enumerated powers effectively.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper's council passes a rule; the queen beekeeper vetoes it; how can council still enact?

options.text: The rule applies after thirty days

questions.explanation: A veto can be overridden by a two-thirds vote in both chambers, preserving legislative power against executive rejection.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook dispute reaches a judge who voids a rule conflicting with the charter; what is this?

options.text: Executive privilege shields the queen beekeeper
Judicial review lets courts invalidate conflicting laws

questions.explanation: Judicial review empowers courts to strike laws conflicting with the Constitution, keeping other branches within bounds.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper's committee revises a proposed rule before full vote; what is this stage?

answer.exemplar: Committee markup is the process where a legislative committee debates, amends, and revises a bill before sending it to the full chamber.

questions.explanation: Markup lets experts refine legislation. It adds detail and can reshape proposals before floor votes.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT

stimulus.body: A presidential veto can be overridden by a two-thirds vote in both the House and the Senate. This requires broad bipartisan support.

questions.stem: A beekeeper's council needs what vote to override the queen's veto?
questions.explanation: Override requires two-thirds in both House and Senate, ensuring broad support. Simple majorities are insufficient.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper rotates hive inspections so not all colonies are checked at once; what purpose do staggered Senate terms serve?

options.text: They make every seat open every two years
They ensure continuity and prevent total turnover
They give the president full control

questions.explanation: Staggered terms ensure institutional continuity and prevent complete turnover. Only one-third of seats open each cycle.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook charges a hive manager; House impeaches, then what?
questions.explanation: The House impeaches; the Senate tries and can remove. This two-stage process separates accusation from judgment.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper's council must approve the queen's appointments; what is this power?

answer.exemplar: Advice and consent requires Senate approval of presidential appointments and treaties, checking executive power through legislative review.

questions.explanation: The Senate's approval role checks the president's appointment and treaty powers, balancing branches.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT

stimulus.body: Treaties require two-thirds approval in the Senate. This high threshold ensures broad consensus on international commitments.

questions.stem: A beekeeper's council needs what vote to ratify a honey trade treaty?
questions.explanation: Treaties require two-thirds Senate approval, ensuring broad consensus. The House does not vote on treaties.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper's council declares a pest war while the queen commands hives; who does what?

options.text: President declares war; Congress commands forces
Congress declares war; president commands forces

questions.explanation: Congress declares war while the president commands military forces. This divides war-making authority.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook names the lead coordinator of the lower chamber; who is this?

options.text: The vice president leads the House
The chief justice leads the House
The Speaker of the House leads the chamber

questions.explanation: The Speaker leads the House, sets agenda, and is second in presidential succession. The vice president presides over the Senate.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper's council can limit court size and jurisdiction; how does Congress check courts?

answer.exemplar: Congress can set court structure, jurisdiction, and impeachment, checking judicial power while preserving judicial review and independence.

questions.explanation: Congress shapes courts through structure and jurisdiction. It cannot easily remove judges, protecting independence.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT

stimulus.body: Extended debate in the Senate can delay legislation. Cloture ends debate with a supermajority vote, allowing a final vote.

questions.stem: A beekeeper's council uses what vote to end endless discussion?

options.text: Cloture ends debate with a supermajority

questions.explanation: Cloture ends extended debate with a supermajority, balancing deliberation with decision. Simple majorities are insufficient.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper's council and queen belong to opposing factions; what often results?
questions.explanation: Divided control often produces gridlock as branches clash. It can also force compromise or inaction.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper's queen issues a directive; what limits it?

options.text: It can override any law freely
It needs no basis at all
It must rest on constitutional or statutory authority

questions.explanation: Executive orders must rest on constitutional or statutory authority and can be overturned by courts or Congress. They are not unlimited.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Apply judicial review to federal conflicts
questions.stem: A beekeeper's regional rule conflicts with central charter; how does judicial review help?

answer.exemplar: Judicial review lets courts resolve conflicts by invalidating laws that violate the Constitution, ensuring uniform interpretation of federal authority.

questions.explanation: Courts settle federal-state conflicts by applying constitutional supremacy. This maintains national uniformity.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT

stimulus.body: Requiring passage through two chambers with different constituencies slows legislation. This design encourages deliberation and compromise.

questions.stem: A beekeeper's two-chamber council slows a new rule; what benefit follows?
questions.explanation: Bicameralism slows legislation to encourage deliberation and compromise. It prevents hasty decisions.

provenance.author: bank-team-us-government
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A beekeeper's lower chamber must start all fee bills; why?

options.text: The queen originates all revenue bills
Revenue bills must originate in the Senate
Revenue bills must originate in the House

questions.explanation: The Constitution requires revenue bills to originate in the House, keeping taxing power close to the people.
